hints: Express $\sum x$ in terms of the mean $\bar{x} = 11.5$ and sample size $n$ as $\sum x = 11.5n$.
Substitute into the equation $11.5n - 10n = 27$ and solve for $n$.
walkthrough:
Expand the linear shift summation property:
$$\sum (x - 10) = \sum x - 10n = 27$$

Use the relation between the mean and total sum $\sum x = n\bar{x} = 11.5n$:
$$11.5n - 10n = 27$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Method 1: Using sums
Step 1: Expand the coded summation.
Over $n$ observations, subtracting a constant $10$ from each observation gives:
$$\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - 10) = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i - \sum_{i=1}^n 10 = \sum x - 10n$$
We are given that this coded sum is $27$:
$$\sum x - 10n = 27$$

Step 2: Connect $\sum x$ with the given mean $\bar{x} = 11.5$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n} \implies \sum x = 11.5n$$

Step 3: Substitute and solve for $n$:
$$11.5n - 10n = 27$$
$$1.5n = 27$$
$$n = \frac{27}{1.5} = 18$$

Method 2: Using the mean of coded data
Dividing the coded sum by $n$ gives the mean of the coded variable $(x - 10)$:
$$\overline{x - 10} = \bar{x} - 10 = 11.5 - 10 = 1.5$$
Since $\overline{x - 10} = \frac{\sum(x - 10)}{n}$:
$$1.5 = \frac{27}{n} \implies n = \frac{27}{1.5} = 18$$
